Radiology Division | Catharina Ziekenhuis, Eindhoven | 20 Feb 2025 | Exam: Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical context points to re-evaluation following a previously negative biopsy. Current prostate-specific antigen measures 0.76 ng/mL, building upon a prior PI-RADS 4 designation.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 36.0 mL in volume, exhibiting asymmetric enlargement. A focal hypointense focus occupies the right peripheral zone at the mid-gland posterior aspect, spanning roughly 12 x 8 x 10 mm. Diffusion-weighted sequences reveal pronounced restricted diffusion alongside correspondingly low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early focal enhancement compared to adjacent parenchyma. Extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle invasion are absent. Pelvic lymph nodes appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right mid-peripheral zone.
PSAD: 0.02 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.39141726

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical review focused on tracking a previously elevated prostate-specific antigen. A prior systematic biopsy returned negative results. The measured value climbed to 0.6 ng/mL, prompting a urology referral for deeper assessment. The individual notes ongoing lower urinary tract symptoms, explicitly ruling out haematuria or bone pain.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Scheduled monitoring tracked the prostate-specific antigen trend. The preceding measurement held steady at 0.4 ng/mL. No symptoms of acute urinary retention were reported. Lower urinary tract symptoms required only conservative management through lifestyle adjustments.
